hadith:
Shortening the Prayers (At-Taqseer) - Narrated Anas bin Malik:

Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) started on a journey before noon, he used to delay the Zuhr prayers till the time for the 'Asr prayer and then he would dismount and offer them together; and whenever the sun declined before he started on a journey he used to offer the Zuhr prayers and then ride (for journey).
message: When we mock Allah's signs or speak carelessly about faith, we risk losing our belief—yet Allah, Al Afuww (The Forgiver), stands ready to pardon those who genuinely repent and turn back to Him. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) adjusted his prayers wisely during travel, we too must navigate life with sincere hearts and mindful words, remembering that Allah sees what is hidden within us. Let this be a reminder to guard our tongues, seek forgiveness, and trust in Allah's boundless mercy.
name:
Al Afuww - العَفُوُّ - The Forgiver

The concept of Al Afuww signifies Allah's readiness to forgive and His compassion towards His creatures. The name is derived from the Arabic root 'عَفَا' (ʿafā), which means to pardon or to overlook. This name is often invoked in prayers and supplications, reflecting the hope for divine mercy and forgiveness. It teaches believers the importance of repentance and the potential for redemption.
verse:
At-Tawbah - The Repentance - 9:64-66

The hypocrites fear that a sûrah should be revealed about them, exposing what is in their hearts. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Keep mocking! Allah will definitely bring to light what you fear.”

If you question them, they will certainly say, “We were only talking idly and joking around.” Say, “Was it Allah, His revelations, and His Messenger that you ridiculed?”

Make no excuses! You have lost faith after your belief. If We pardon a group of you, We will punish others for their wickedness.
